meta.title: Phadke Shree Ganpati
meta.institution: The Yashodabai Govind Gangadhar Phadke Charitable Trust
meta.location: Phadke Wadi, Vithalbhai Patel Road, opposite Sikka Nagar, Girgaon, Mumbai 400004
meta.foundedNote: The temple’s history says construction was completed around 1890; its organizational account dates idol installation to 1890. Treat this as a retrospective approximate construction date, not a recovered consecration certificate.
meta.intro: Phadke Shree Ganpati is a permanent temple in Girgaon’s Phadkewadi. Its history centres on Yashodabai Phadke’s patronage, a lotus-seated Ganesh accompanied by Riddhi-Siddhi and a Ganesh Panchayatan, and the later work of a charitable trust. Alongside temple and festival history, this collection includes dated photographs of the trust’s community service. It is separate from similarly named Phadke temples in Pune.

paragraphs.text: The temple’s Marathi history says Govind Gangadhar Phadke moved from Awas near Alibag to Mumbai in 1865 and bought land in 1867. After his death, Yashodabai directed her resources toward a Ganesh temple; construction was completed around 1890. The account links the names Govindbagh and Phadkewadi to that family estate. It is the institution’s retrospective narrative, not a surviving nineteenth-century deed inspected here.

sections.title: Ganesh Panchayatan in a silver setting

paragraphs.text: The north-facing temple contains a seated Ganesh on a lotus, with the trunk leaning left, Riddhi-Siddhi beside him and silver ornament around the shrine. Pilgrim Data’s multilingual survey describes a hall, sanctum and circumambulatory route, while the temple history identifies the accompanying Panchayatan deities as Mahalakshmi, Vishnu, Shiva and Surya. The original artisan’s personal name is not established in the inspected record.

The gallery's original-resolution image reveals the continuing Ganesh with Riddhi-Siddhi, silver lion-sided seating, garlands and leaves. It supplies no capture date. A separate ritual sequence preserves Nikon camera dates in May 2019, although the files were processed in 2020 and placed in a 2024 upload folder. Those photographs show a small metal Ganesh handled during worship; they do not establish the making or installation of a new main temple idol.

The organization dates legal establishment of its charitable trust to 21 January 1922. Its account groups work into religious, social and educational programmes: daily worship, Maghi Ganesh Janmotsav, Bhadrapad Ganeshotsav and Gauri Puja sit alongside scholarships, educational supplies and food assistance. These are institutional descriptions; quoted beneficiary totals have not been independently audited and are not projected forward as current figures.

A specific institutional report documents food distribution at Yashomangal hall on 20 October 2023, supporting two photographs of that event. The dated community record matters separately from images of the deity. In Girgaon’s public calendar, the temple also serves as the starting point of the Gudi Padwa Hindu Navvarsh Swagat Yatra, as described in a 2024 local report.

The temple history dates electrification to 1918 and construction of the Yashomangal building to 1959-60. It describes the latter as space for marriages, religious functions and meetings. These are episodes in the development of a continuing temple complex. Photographs in this collection do not imply that its central Ganesh is recreated and immersed annually.

claims.text: Yashodabai’s temple construction was completed around 1890 according to institutional history.
The trust gives 21 January 1922 as its legal establishment date.
The central icon is a permanent lotus-seated Ganesh with associated Panchayatan deities.
The two dated photographs document a 2023 food-distribution event, not temple consecration or annual icon production.
